events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.83)
events.body:
The trip is a RydeX fixed-quote booking: the fare of $24.93 is composed of listed components (base $3.90, distance $15.06 for 10.68 km, time $4.50 for 17.3 min, waiting $0.00, platform $1.47) [F6], and the billed distance of 10.7 km does not exceed the optimal 10.7 km [F4]. Under RD-2 the non-metered branch refunds only ERP/tolls generated on an unexcused segment and any unpublished post-trip add-on; the extra mileage itself does not move a fixed quote, and no such item appears in the bill [F6]. The recoverable amount is therefore $0.00, so the fare outcome is no_action while the RD-1 breach is recorded [RD-2].

The GPS record shows a genuine unexcused deviation: one off-route segment 14:19–14:26 drove 5.03 km where the optimal route covers 1.39 km, adding 3.64 km and straying up to 1160 m from the optimal route [F3], in a trip that ran 15.2 km against 10.7 km optimal (+4.5 km, +42%) [F1]. RD-1 sets no percentage or absolute km threshold, so this segment violates the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty unless RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 excuses it [RD-1].

RD-5 does not excuse it. There is no in-app chat traffic at all [F7], so no rider message sent before 14:19 authorised a route change or a stop; the driver's post-trip explanation that "the GPS rerouted me" [F8] is a statement, not rider consent, and a driver's claim of agreement cannot supply the rider's own prior message [RD-5]. actions.detail: account action is never automatic; queued for Ryde review

what_would_change: Had an LTA incident been recorded on the stretch F3 replaced, before it started, RD-4 would exempt it (fixed fare: no amount changes, the RD-1 breach would not be recorded).

claims.assertion: The GPS record shows the driver covered 15.2 km against a 10.7 km optimal route, +4.5 km (+42%), and 23.2 min against an estimated 17.3 min (+5.9 min).

One off-route segment is recorded: 14:19-14:26, 5.03 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.39 km, adding 3.64 km and straying up to 1160 m from the optimal route, an unexplained deviation under RD-1.

No in-app chat message exists at all, so no rider message before 14:19 named a road, agreed to a route change, or authorised any stop; the segment therefore has no rider consent before it began (consent_after_or_none).

The driver's only explanation is a post-trip statement, 'The GPS rerouted me', a claim untethered to any record of a road, stop or incident; a driver's statement cannot supply the consent that RD-5 requires from the rider's own message.

RD-4 offers the driver no cover: traffic facts show only speed band 4 (30-39 km/h) on AYE and CTE, which is neither band 1 nor band 2, and no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window; weather was fair, so no severe-congestion or road-block excuse is evidenced.

Because the service was RydeX (fixed quote) the billed distance stayed at the optimal 10.7 km and no detour mileage reached the fare, so the monetary refund on the non-metered branch is nil and the outcome on the fare is no_action.

The case nonetheless records a driver breach of the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty: one unexcused off-route segment adding 3.64 km with a 1160 m maximum stray, and the driver's own 90-day history shows 4 disputes with 2 route disputes upheld, so RD-6's repeated condition is met on this record.

weaknesses: The fare facts are against my client on money: billed distance 10.68 km equals the optimal 10.7 km, so on the non-metered RydeX branch RD-2 yields a recoverable amount of 0 and F4/F6 support the driver's 'nothing wrong with the fare'.
F1 shows 4.5 km excess in total while the single recorded segment (F3) accounts for 3.64 km; the remaining roughly 0.9 km is corridor wobble that RD-2 does not refund even on a metered trip.
The rider has 2 prior disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld (F13), which the driver may use to suggest a pattern of fee complaints.

There is no chat record at all (F7), so I cannot show any rider message either way; the driver's 'GPS rerouted me' statement (F8) is the only account of why the route was taken, and speed band 4 congestion on AYE/CTE (F9, F10) gives it some colour even though it fails RD-4's band 1/2 threshold.

claims.assertion: The trip was a RydeX fixed-quote service: the fare of $24.93 is composed only of the quoted components (base $3.90, distance $15.06, time $4.50, waiting $0.00, platform $1.47) and the billed distance of 10.7 km does not exceed the optimal route of 10.7 km, so no money is attributable to the off-route segment.

The only off-route segment (14:19–14:26) added 3.64 km of driving, but on a non-metered RydeX booking mileage does not change the fare, so the recoverable amount under RD-2 is zero and the correct outcome is no_action.
No ERP/toll or post-trip unpublished charge appears anywhere in the bill — waiting is $0.00 and the total equals the sum of the listed components — so FARE-1/FARE-2 give the rider nothing to recover.

There is no in-app chat traffic at all, so the rider never named a road or a stop and never objected during the segment; the driver's post-trip explanation of a GPS reroute is a statement only and is not offered as, and cannot be, rider consent.

The driver cannot invoke the RD-4 traffic exemption: the only traffic records are speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on the AYE and CTE, which is neither an incident nor a band 1–2 condition, and no incident was recorded near the route during the trip window.

The rider's own account is clean on route conduct (0 of 2 disputes upheld in 90 days), which is consistent with a genuinely unexplained deviation; nonetheless the driver's 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days are profile facts that go only to any account-review action, not to whether this segment was excused.

weaknesses: The 42% overshoot is stark and the driver has no excuse for it: F1 (+4.5 km) and F3 (3.64 km added, up to 1160 m off the optimal route) are system records the judge will read against us, and RD-1 sets no threshold that could rescue a deviation of this size.

My own claim D5 concedes the RD-4 defence fails: F11 records no traffic incident and F9/F10 are only band 4, so the segment stands as an unexcused off-route segment and RD-1 is breached on the record.

F14 shows the driver already has 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, so RD-6's 'repeated' condition is met on the driver's side and a flag_account referral may be added even though the fare claim fails.

RD-2's premise that a fixed quote protects the driver is a fares argument only; if the judge treats the recorded breach of RD-1 as a finding in itself, the rider achieves the 'on record' outcome he asked for with no monetary change, and F7's empty chat log leaves the driver with no consent evidence whatsoever.

points.response: Conceded on the money: on this fixed-quote RydeX booking nothing in the bill moves with distance (F4, F6), so I claim no refund of the fare. The rider's complaint was expressly that the detour be put on record, not that he was overcharged.

Conceded that RD-2 yields SGD 0 of recoverable mileage here (F3, F6), but RD-2's own final sentence records the RD-1 breach when the refundable amount is zero, so D2 does not erase the off-route segment: F3 stands as an unexcused 3.64 km deviation, 1160 m off the optimal route.
Accepted: the bill contains no ERP/toll or unpublished post-trip item (F6, F5), so FARE-1 and FARE-2 give the rider nothing, and the outcome stays no_action on the fare.

Conceded as far as it goes: with no chat traffic (F7) the rider never named a road or stop, and the driver's 'GPS rerouted me' statement (F8) is a claim, not rider consent under RD-5; but the same emptiness leaves the segment with no consent at all, i.e. consent_after_or_none, and RD-3 cannot rescue an unnaming stop that produced no named place.

Conceded: band 4 (30-39 km/h) on AYE/CTE is neither band 1 nor 2, and no incident was recorded near the route during the trip window (F9, F10, F11, F12), so the segment is unexcused under RD-1/RD-4 exactly as the driver's own brief now admits.

The driver's concession controls: with the segment unexcused, the rider's requested 'detour on record' is achieved by the finding of the RD-1 breach itself, which carries no money on a fixed quote; as both briefs agree, F14 (2 route disputes upheld in 90 days) goes only to a flag_account referral under RD-6, never to deciding this segment.

Agreed, and this is the crux both advocates now state: F4 and F6 show the billed 10.68 km does not exceed the optimal 10.7 km and the $24.93 total contains no detour mileage, so RD-2's non-metered branch leaves a recoverable amount of 0 and the fare outcome is no_action.
